content:
alex.k: quick helm question — trying to stash a multiline private key in values.yaml and render it into a Kubernetes Secret, then read it from a container via valueFrom.secretKeyRef. helm/templating keeps turning newlines into literal \n sequences and my app sees backslash-n instead of real newlines. anyone hit this?

 tasha: can you paste the values.yaml snippet + the secret template you use? also are you passing the key via CI/terraform or checked into repo?

 alex.k: sure — values.yaml (simplified):
 ```yaml
 jwtKey: |
   -----BEGIN RSA PRIVATE KEY-----
   MIIEowIBAAKCAQE...rest
   -----END RSA PRIVATE KEY-----
 ```
 helm template snippet (templates/secret.yaml):
 ```yaml
 apiVersion: v1
 kind: Secret
 metadata:
   name: {{ .Release.Name }}-jwt
 type: Opaque
 data:
   jwt_key: {{ .Values.jwtKey | b64enc }}
 ```
 container env in deployment (templates/deployment.yaml):
 ```yaml
 - name: JWT_KEY
   valueFrom:
     secretKeyRef:
       name: {{ .Release.Name }}-jwt
       key: jwt_key
 ```

 ben: couple quick things — that flow should work. kubernetes secrets are binary-safe, base64 preserves newlines. if your app is seeing literal \n then most likely the value was injected with literal backslash-n (eg via JSON encoding) or you used YAML folded style `>` which collapses newlines. use `|` as you showed.
 also helm templating sometimes adds unexpected quoting; try: 
 ```yaml
 jwt_key: {{ .Values.jwtKey | b64enc | quote }}
 ```
 that ensures the rendered YAML value is a quoted string and avoids extra escaping in some renderers.

 priya: another common gotcha — if you pass the key via `--set` (or terraform helm provider set values) you lose multiline semantics. `helm upgrade --set jwtKey="$(cat key.pem)"` turns newlines into literal `\n`. prefer `--set-file jwtKey=path` or provide a values file.

 alex.k: ah ok — i'm actually deploying via terraform (helm_release provider) and we pass sensitive values with set-like args in the module, so that explains it.

 ben: yep terraform helm provider behaves like `--set`. options:
 - use helm_release.values = [file("./ci/generated-values.yaml")] (generate a file at CI time)
 - create the k8s_secret with the terraform kubernetes provider using `filebase64("path/to/key.pem")` and have the chart read an existing secret name
 example TF snippet: 
 ```hcl
 resource "helm_release" "app" {
   name = "my-app"
   chart = "./chart"
   values = [file("./ci/generated-values.yaml")]
 }
 ```
 or: 
 ```hcl
 resource "kubernetes_secret" "jwt" {
   metadata { name = "my-app-jwt" }
   data = { jwt_key = filebase64("path/to/key.pem") }
 }
 ```

 chart-bot: chart-lint: INFO — templates/secret.yaml missing `type: Opaque` in a few branches (not blocking)

 alex.k: thanks all — switching to generating a values file in CI (or creating the secret via k8s provider) to preserve newlines. will report back after I try. :thumbsup: 

 tasha: fwiw we have an infra example for this in infra/common/helm/README.md if you need it.

 alex.k: got it, thanks everyone!
